source_text: [1] Εὐχαριστίας καὶ πρυσευχῆς ἀπέχονται, διὰ τὸ μὴ ὁμολογεῖν τὴν εὐχαριστίαν σάρκα εἶναι τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τὴν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν παθοῦσαν, ἣν τῇ χρηστότητι ὁ πατὴρ ἤγειρεν. οἱ οὖν ἀντιλέγοντες τῇ δωρεᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ συζητοῦντες ἀποθνήσκουσιν: συνέφερεν δε αὐτοῖς ἀγαπᾶν, ἵνα καὶ ἀναστῶσιν. [2] πρέπον ἐστὶν ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν τοιούτων καὶ μήτε κατ’ ἰδίαν περὶ αὐτῶν λαλεῖν μήτε κοινῇ, προσέχειν δὲ τοῖς προφήταις, ἐξαιρέτως δὲ τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ, ἐν ᾧ τὸ πάθος ἡμῖν δεδήλωται καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις τετελείωται. τοὺς δὲ μερισμοὺς φεύγετε ὡς ἀρχὴν κακῶν.
pass_a_gloss: [1] They keep away from the Eucharist and from prayer, because they do not confess that the Eucharist is the flesh of our Savior Jesus Christ, which suffered for our sins, which the Father raised in his goodness. So those who speak against the gift of God die in their disputing. It would be better for them to love, so that they might also rise. [2] It is fitting to keep away from such people and not to speak about them either in private or in public, but to pay attention to the prophets, and especially to the gospel, in which the passion has been made plain to us and the resurrection has been brought to completion. Flee divisions as the beginning of evils.
pass_b_english: They stay away from the Eucharist and from prayer, because they will not confess that the Eucharist is the flesh of our Savior Jesus Christ. That flesh suffered for our sins. That flesh the Father in his kindness raised. Those who argue against God's gift die arguing. They would do better to love, so that they too might rise.

So it is right to stay clear of such people and not talk about them, privately or publicly. Give your attention to the prophets, and above all to the gospel. There the passion has been shown to us, and the resurrection made complete. Run from divisions. They are where evil begins.

choices.why: Ignatius's flat predication kept; the following relative clauses are split into two 'That flesh…' sentences for his hammer rhythm.
The plain verb; some take it as 'hold the love feast'. ANF's 'treat it with respect' is not the sense of the verb.
Participle of manner as a short burst.
rejected: incur death in the midst of their disputes (ANF; wordy)

anf_compare.notes: ANF renders ἀγαπᾶν 'to treat it with respect' and τετελείωται 'fully proved'; the Greek says 'to love' and 'brought to completion'. Rest same sense.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] is Smyrnaeans 7. Greek «Εὐχαριστίας καὶ πρυσευχῆς ἀπέχονται, διὰ τὸ μὴ ὁμολογεῖν τὴν εὐχαριστίαν σάρκα εἶναι τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ» matches Pass A «They keep away from the Eucharist and from prayer, because they do not confess that the Eucharist is the flesh of our Savior Jesus Christ» and Pass B «They stay away from the Eucharist and from prayer, because they will not confess that the Eucharist is the flesh of our Savior Jesus Christ». Modifiers «τὴν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν παθοῦσαν, ἣν τῇ χρηστότητι ὁ πατὴρ ἤγειρεν» stay in A («which suffered for our sins, which the Father raised in his goodness») and are kept by B’s anaphora («That flesh suffered for our sins. That flesh the Father in his kindness raised») without weakening «σάρκα εἶναι» to representation. «οἱ οὖν ἀντιλέγοντες τῇ δωρεᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ συζητοῦντες ἀποθνήσκουσιν» = A «those who speak against the gift of God die in their disputing» / B «Those who argue against God's gift die arguing». «συνέφερεν δε αὐτοῖς ἀγαπᾶν, ἵνα καὶ ἀναστῶσιν» is love so as to rise in both. Section [2] in the same paragraph, «πρέπον ἐστὶν ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν τοιούτων καὶ μήτε κατ’ ἰδίαν περὶ αὐτῶν λαλεῖν μήτε κοινῇ» through «τοὺς δὲ μερισμοὺς φεύγετε ὡς ἀρχὴν κακῶν», is covered; B «They are where evil begins» does not reverse A «as the beginning of evils». Typo «πρυσευχῆς» is disclosed. No false citation. Title names the flesh-predication.

Source identity confirmed: Ignatius, Smyrnaeans 7, matches Locked Greek. Completeness: all clauses from both paragraphs rendered; no omission of arguments, qualifications, or quotations. Negation: 'οὐ ὁμολογεῖν' correctly rendered as 'do not confess' / 'will not confess'. Agency: clear that heterodox 'keep away', 'speak against', and 'die'; orthodox duty to 'keep away', 'pay attention', 'flee'. Modality: 'πρέπον ἐστὶν' → 'It is fitting' / 'So it is right'; 'συμφέρει' → 'It would be better' / 'They would do better'; ἵνα clauses → 'so that' constructions. Doctrine: real flesh of Christ, his suffering, resurrection, and rejection of docetism preserved. Scripture: no explicit citations in Locked Greek; added identification of 'gift of God' as possible John 4:10 echo is properly noted as unmarked per rule. Title 'The Eucharist Is His Flesh' names the thought. Covered source paragraphs: [1]. No uncertainties; translation choices align with lemmas and choices. Pass A and B convey same sense; no contradiction or addition. Minor stylistic differences (e.g., 'raised in his goodness' vs 'the Father in his kindness raised'; 'brought to completion' vs 'made complete'; 'flee' vs 'run from') are within acceptable bounds. No fail triggers.
